title: This Robot Hand Walks on Its Fingers Like a Creepy Thing
summary:
Halloween is coming, and engineers have made a robot hand that looks like a creepy character from The Addams Family. That character is a walking hand named Thing. This new robot hand can balance on its fingertips and creep around on its own. It can tap keyboard keys, push small objects and even play a simple computer game while balancing on its other fingers.

Engineers have built walking robot hands before, but they had to make every finger the same length so the hand could balance. Real human hands have fingers of different lengths and a thumb on the opposite side. That uneven shape makes standing upright hard.

A team from the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich in Switzerland wanted to solve this problem. They wrote about their work in a preprint, which is a paper that has not yet been checked by other scientists or published in a journal. The team started with a mechanical hand made for humanoid robots. It has five fingers and 20 moving joints. They added a battery, motion sensors and a tiny computer on the back. The whole hand weighs 1.8 pounds.

The team taught the hand to balance inside a computer simulation using reinforcement learning. The software gave the hand a reward every time it balanced correctly. Then it walked across carpet, gravel, grass and metal in 14 different indoor and outdoor places. In one test, it hit the correct keys on a keyboard 29 out of 32 times. It even played a puzzle video game called Sokoban by pressing the right arrow keys in order.

The team says this could be useful one day. A humanoid robot working in a tight space might detach its hand and send it crawling to grab an item.
why_it_matters: Teaching robot hands to balance and move on their own could help future robots do tasks in places that are hard to reach.
